Status: Wave 316 accepted (6.3): the DeviceInfo sections and the general section's accessors

Method.evidence: Five type rows and the general section's 31 accessor rows. The four DeviceInfo section classes match 6.4 field for field and in order: Class479 = IoTApplicationProgramSection (IDataProvider, (ushort,ushort,byte) application-program id, IoTLoadStateMachineState, ulong fingerprint, id formatter), Class480 = IoTGeneralSection (sixteen fields following 6.4's IDataProvider, InstallationId?, IndividualAddress?, ushort?, SerialNumber?, string?, Version, bool?, Version, string?, string?, string?, Version, IEnumerable<IPAddress>?, ushort?, ushort?), Class481 = IoTGroupCommunicationSection (group-object/recipient/publisher collections, per-table XElement builders, ConfigurationFlags formatting) and Class483 = IoTDeviceInfo (List<Class478> with ToXml). Class485 is Tasks.CompareDevice.IoTDeviceComparer by its four collaborators and the IoTCompareDeviceStage state. The 31 accessors are the special-name getter/setter pairs of the general section, position by position against 6.4's property list, so they take get_/set_ names for InstallationId, IndividualAddress, DeviceManufacturerId, SerialNumber, HardwareType, FirmwareVersion, ProgrammingMode, ApiVersion, BasePath, Model, Hostname, HardwareVersion, IPv6Addresses, Port and MulticastPort plus the private data-provider getter.
Method.themes: The DeviceInfo subsystem is readable now, and the section accessors give dnSpy the get_/set_ pairs it needs to show those fields as properties. Deliberately unresolved: Class478 and Class482, the section base and the router-IPv4/group-address-mapping section, are obfuscated in 6.4 too (Sections.Class185/Class186), so no vendor name exists for them; Class485's task method returns Task<object> with no 6.4 counterpart and stays free.
